 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 MS Dhoni's future with Chennai Super Kings is a major talking point ahead of the IPL 2027 retention deadline.
 Several CSK fans believe the former India captain may have retired, interpreting social media posts and online claims as signs.
 Dhoni's IPL 2027 participation remains uncertain, with no official confirmation of his retirement or a mentoring role.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE: CSK retention list for IPL 2027: Retained and released players 
 MS Dhoni retirement rumours leave CSK fans anxious ahead of IPL 2027 auction
 Dhoni's future in professional cricket is back in the limelight due to the apprehensions being raised by Chennai Super Kings fans about the impending retirement of the wicket-keeper batter ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction.
 Multiple posts on social media have started rumours that the legendary cricketer might have decided to retire from the game, and some believe that he can carry forward his association with CSK through mentorship.
 It has been rumored that MS Dhoni may retire from professional cricket on November 17.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Nevertheless, there has been no official statement released either by MS Dhoni or CSK about his retirement from professional cricket.
 MORE: IPL retention vs release vs trade: What is the difference? 
 What are CSK fans saying about MS Dhoni's retirement?
 Social media is flooded with emotional responses from CSK fans with some users even stating that they are preparing themselves for Dhoni's retirement.
 A fan user wrote an emotionally charged message with the simple caption: "Dhoni 💔", while another questioned whether Dhoni will retire on November 17th.
 Another fan user paid an emotional tribute to Dhoni , saying that he was the one who has given CSK its identity and got millions of people hooked to cricket through his performance.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "i just know that I will cry my heart out tom at 5 Thankyou Thala 💛 #CSK," the user mentioned.
 On the other hand, a CSK fan urged Dhoni to play one last match in the MA Chidambaram Stadium before retiring, stating: "We are wasting so many crores on useless players, we can waste 4 more crores for one match. You have given a word that you will play your last match at Chepauk. Please play one more match, take a farewell and retire @msdhoni"
 Also, there were rumours floating around that Dhoni had already retired from professional cricket but will continue his association with CSK as a mentor.
 MORE: IPL 2027: Three teams that can sign Aaryavir Sehwag at the mini-auction 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement What has MS Dhoni said about playing in IPL 2027?
 Dhoni's participation in the IPL 2027 season has been in limbo since he failed to take part in any game of IPL 2026 owing to fitness-related concerns, in particular with regard to his calf.
 While addressing a healthcare conference in Bengaluru in October, the 45-year-old made it clear that he would consider his own fitness levels before making a decision regarding his participation in another season.
 "Doc, I will have to go through the test. You will have to give me the report, and then before December, I will have to see, you know, how strong I am to maybe play one more season," he said.
 He added humorously that he needed medical help to keep his "old vintage vehicle" working perfectly, thereby indicating that it would all depend on his body's capacity to take up another IPL season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Thus, his remarks offered some respite to the CSK fans as they realised that he had not yet shut the door on participating in IPL 2027.
 MORE: CSK's coaching staff, IPL 2027: Full list of coaches and support staff 
 Will CSK retain MS Dhoni for IPL 2027 mini-auction?
 CSK are yet to announce their retention list ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction, and the deadline is on November 17. The future of Dhoni is still a huge topic of discussion, especially after the recent changes in the squad of the franchise, which involved a deal with Sunrisers Hyderabad involving four players to bring Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards to Chennai.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement If Dhoni does not want to play another season in the tournament, a mentoring role would be a natural step as the franchise can make use of his expertise and leadership. Apart from the five IPL titles won as captain, Dhoni has been instrumental in shaping the franchise's identity and in creating a strong bond between himself and CSK fans.
 But officially, there has not been any announcement regarding his retirement from cricket or a change of roles. It is time that the franchise or Dhoni should clarify this issue, as the legendary wicketkeeper deserves a proper farewell at Chepauk.
